AMSC should be retained as the most direct US-listed small-cap candidate for grid-stability and power-quality equipment because of D-VAR/STATCOM exposure; survival depends on proving current revenue/backlog exposure rather than relying on older deployment history.

POWL is a useful adjacent electrical-infrastructure candidate but is above the preferred market-cap range and increasingly visible; classify as underfollowed only relative to mega-cap electrical leaders, not relative to PLPC/AMSC.

For US-listed equities, pure-play HVDC reactor and HVDC CTC magnet-wire exposure appears thin. The investable public lane likely maps to adjacent T&D hardware, STATCOM/reactive-power systems, switchgear/control systems, bushings, arresters, substations, and grid-protection/control components.

PLPC is a second-order transmission-hardware candidate rather than an HVDC reactor supplier; include it in future passes when searching physical transmission bill-of-material bottlenecks, especially spacer dampers, conductor protection, substation fittings and line hardware.

HMDPF/HPS.A is relevant to the magnetics and power-quality branch, but direct HVDC/high-voltage reactor exposure is unverified and must be treated as a hypothesis until technical voltage-rating and customer evidence is found.

Need a separate non-US listed search for Quality Power Electrical Equipments, CTC magnet wire, HVDC reactor suppliers, bushing/capacitor vendors, and India/Europe/Japan/Korea suppliers; US-listed universe appears thin for pure HVDC reactor exposure.

AMSC should remain in the underfollowed lane for grid-stability equipment due to direct D-VAR STATCOM/reactive-power exposure; validate current Grid segment backlog and customer concentration before promotion.
ALNT is a hidden power-quality candidate through TCI; the key gating item is segment-level revenue/backlog disclosure for harmonic filters, reactors, and power-quality systems.

PLPC is not a reactor/power-electronics supplier but is a plausible second-order transmission-hardware beneficiary; evidence should focus on utility transmission exposure and procurement lead-time advantage.

Clean US-listed magnet-wire or HVDC CTC magnet-wire exposure was not found in this pass. Quality Power Electrical Equipments is a relevant India-listed discovery lead from external context but does not satisfy the US-listed filter.
The node splits into at least three investable sub-lanes: utility-scale capacitor/reactor incumbents, dynamic reactive-power/grid-stability systems, and second-order transmission-line hardware.

AMSC is the strongest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the grid-stability / high-voltage power-quality subnode because D-VAR STATCOM exposure maps directly to voltage stability, reactive-power support, power-factor correction, and renewable interconnection.
PLPC is a second-order transmission hardware candidate rather than a direct HVDC-reactor candidate; it should be tracked as an early-procurement BOM supplier for transmission and EHV buildout.

For US-listed equities, the most investable public mappings to this node appear to be STATCOM/reactive-power equipment, transmission-line hardware, and power capacitors rather than pure HVDC reactors or HVDC CTC magnet wire.

Direct HVDC reactor and backward-integrated HVDC CTC magnet-wire suppliers appear more likely to be found outside primary US listings; later passes should examine India, Canada, Europe, Japan, Korea, and OTC ADRs while checking liquidity and disclosure quality.
